tasks.spec:
You are being consulted as an ADVISOR, not as a worker. Write advice; do not change any system.

WHY YOU (audit record): the operator invoked the Fable red phone by name. This is a judgment call about process design, not a coding task. Two prior model-authored decisions are in direct conflict, the numeric evidence CANNOT adjudicate between them (it ties), the operator has explicitly said he does not want to 'force things' by simply reverting, and any fix sets a precedent for how two machines stay in sync. That combination -- irreversible-ish precedent, tied evidence, an operator who wants the reasoning rather than the action -- is what the red phone is for.

=== SITUATION ===

The operator runs 'Ringer', a tool that dispatches coding tasks to CLI workers from several model families (OpenAI Codex tiers 'sol/terra/luna', Anthropic 'opus/sonnet', Moonshot 'k3') and verifies every task by EXECUTING a check command. Exit 0 is the only PASS. Every attempt is appended to an eval log (~/.ringer/runs.jsonl, 413 rows) that produces a scoreboard.

Routing doctrine: the unit is a CELL = (model x effort), not a model. Which model AND how hard it thinks are both chosen per task. A canonical routing table lives in ~/.claude/rules/model-routing.md and is loaded into every session.

He has two machines: a Mac (this one) and a Windows laptop. A repo, AustinJunyuLi/ringer, carries an 'overlay/' bundle plus a deploy script that reproduces his whole setup on a new machine -- it OVERWRITES ~/.config/ringer/config.toml, ~/.claude/rules/model-routing.md, and the orchestrator skill, backing up each first.

=== WHAT HAPPENED ===

1. On 2026-07-27 he worked on the WINDOWS machine: retired a lane ('kimiclaude', a Kimi-through-Claude-harness engine) in favour of the native Kimi CLI, and made effort adaptive on every lane. Good work, correctly evidenced, pushed to GitHub.

2. Today he asked me to install that on the Mac. I ran the deploy. It succeeded -- 5/5 lane probe PASS, first attempt.

3. But the Windows machine's copy of the evidence file (docs/MODEL-NOTES.md) was STALE. It stops at 2026-07-22 plus the two new 07-27 entries. Everything from 07-24 and 07-25 is missing from it -- those days' work happened on the Mac and was never pushed.

4. Consequently the deployed routing table silently REVERSED a decision made on 2026-07-25 on the Mac. That decision ('the Opus 5 lane swap') moved substantial code features and architecture review from k3 to Opus. The newly-deployed table sends both back to k3.

5. The operator confirms he did NOT change his mind. The reversal is purely an artifact of the stale copy.

=== WHY THE NUMBERS CANNOT SETTLE IT ===

The 07-25 decision came from a 12-dispatch paired bakeoff (both cells from a byte-identical seed dir, same spec, same hidden executed check, review lanes graded BLIND against planted-defect answer keys).

On EXECUTED CHECKS it was a dead tie:
  bakeoff-feature      opus 2/2 PASS   k3 2/2 PASS
  bakeoff-arch-review  opus 1P/1F      k3 1P/1F
  bakeoff-executor     sonnet 2/2      k3 2/2
  bakeoff-gate-review  sonnet 0/2      k3 1P/1F

The tie was broken by a BLIND SIDE-BY-SIDE CODE READ, whose findings existed only as PROSE in MODEL-NOTES: opus won both feature tasks (shorter -- 84L vs 92L, 82L vs 105L -- and left a runnable self-check on each where k3 left none); k3's task-2 solution indexed by FILE LINE instead of row, so a blank line shifts every subsequent index -- a spec deviation that SURVIVED ITS OWN PASSING CHECK; k3's task-1 used .get('duration_ms', 0), turning a malformed row into a silently wrong median instead of a crash. It also recorded that the premise which had justified k3 on this lane -- 'k3 parsimony is a feature virtue' -- was FALSIFIED, because k3 wrote MORE code, not less, on both tasks.

The newly-deployed table re-justifies k3 on that lane with exactly that falsified premise: 'parsimonious diffs suit feature work'.

So: the scoreboard shows a tie and cannot defend the decision. The artifact that could defend it was prose, and the prose is what got overwritten.

=== THE DEEPER DEFECT (the operator considers this the real point) ===

Routing doctrine says route CELLS = (model x effort). But the eval log can only RECORD the effort half for ONE of three lanes.

The function effective_reasoning_effort_from_command (ringer.py:8805) regex-matches only the Codex argv form 'model_reasoning_effort=<x>'. The Claude lane passes '--effort <x>' and the Kimi lane carries effort in the model alias (k3-low / k3-high / k3-max). Both return None.

Measured over the live log: codex 126 rows with effort logged, 7 null; claude 0 logged, 64 null; kimi 0 logged, 112 null.

This was DISCOVERED AND WRITTEN DOWN on 07-25, with the root cause and line number, as a '~4-line fix'. It is still unfixed. The 07-27 audit that declared 'ALL FOUR LANES ARE ADAPTIVE' verified that dispatch WORKS at each effort, but did not check that the log CAPTURES which effort ran.

So the fleet has just committed to a routing doctrine whose central variable it cannot measure on two thirds of its lanes. Every future 'the scoreboard outranks the table' judgment on a Claude or Kimi lane is being made on half-attributed rows.

Also present, lower stakes: the live eval log still holds 111 rows for deleted 'qwen' lanes and 48 for the deleted kimiclaude harness. One deleted lane ('qwen3.8-max-preview') still displays as 'proven, 15 tasks, 100%' on the scoreboard a boss consults.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===

- The operator does NOT want to 'force things'. He rejected simply reverting the table.
- Everything is recoverable: the 07-24/07-25 notes survive on the Mac in an old checkout; every overwritten file has a timestamped .bak.
- The rules file is loaded into every session, so whatever it says is what actually governs behaviour tomorrow.
- The deploy script is the ONLY sync path between the two machines, and it is one-way: it overwrites the destination.

=== WHAT TO WRITE ===

Write advice.md with EXACTLY these three level-2 headings, in this order, and nothing else at level 2:

## What to do now
The immediate call on the reversed routing decision. Take a POSITION -- do not list options without choosing. The operator has already rejected a plain revert; if you nonetheless think reverting is right, say so and say why his objection is wrong. Address explicitly: is a decision whose only real evidence is a blind prose judgment a decision that SHOULD survive a file sync, or is its fragility telling us something true about how well-founded it was?

## The measurement gap
Your read on the effort-attribution defect. Is the operator right that this is the more important problem? What does it mean that a doctrine was adopted whose key variable is unmeasurable on most lanes -- and that the defect was documented with a line number two days before that doctrine shipped, and still went unfixed? Say what you would do about it and in what order relative to the first section.

## The structural fix
The two-machine sync problem underneath all of this. A one-way overwrite deploy silently reverted a measured decision because one machine's evidence file was stale. Say what should change so this class of failure cannot recur. Be concrete and be honest about cost -- if the honest answer is 'accept this risk, it is cheaper than the fix', say that.

Budget roughly 400-900 words total. Prose, not bullets, wherever a bullet would hide the reasoning. You are advising a competent operator who wants your judgment, not a summary of his own situation back. Disagreeing with him is the most valuable thing you can do here. Write ONLY advice.md in your working directory and create no other files.
tasks.check: bash -c 'test -f advice.md || { echo "FAIL: no advice.md"; ls -la; exit 1; }; for h in "## What to do now" "## The measurement gap" "## The structural fix"; do grep -qF "$h" advice.md || { echo "FAIL: missing heading: $h"; exit 1; }; done; w=$(wc -w < advice.md); test "$w" -ge 300 || { echo "FAIL: only $w words"; exit 1; }; echo "PASS: advice.md, $w words, all 3 sections present"'
tasks.verified: Fable red-phone consult returned an advisory deliverable with all three required sections and substantive length; executed check read it back.
